maria: Heads up — onboarding sampleapp (node) is intermittently dropping the request-id header when the SDK autoinstruments and the log level flips from info->debug during startup. Repro steps below, and I think it's a bootstrap/init ordering race. @liam FYI

maria: Repro (local):
```bash
git clone .../sampleapp
cd sampleapp
npm i
REDWOOD_LOG_LEVEL=debug node server.js
# then hit endpoint /chat with retries enabled
```
Logs show the wrapper emits a new request-id during retry, but downstream traces keep the old trace id. Looks like two places are stamping headers depending on whether telemetry is initialized yet.

liam: ugh. can you paste the exact log snippet and package versions? ffwds to sdk team. also do you see this only with node 18 or node 20 too?

maria: snippet:
```
[2026-03-03T12:04:01.123Z] INFO  server  <-- incoming request { path: "/chat", request-id: "rid-abc123" }
[2026-03-03T12:04:01.128Z] DEBUG retry  retrying request, new request-id set: "rid-xyz789"
[2026-03-03T12:04:01.129Z] DEBUG otel   span started trace-id=abcd1234 request-id=rid-abc123
[2026-03-03T12:04:01.130Z] DEBUG sdk    init complete, request-id reconciled -> rid-xyz789
```
Packages: redwood-telemetry@0.9.2, redwood-sdk@1.4.0, @opentelemetry/api@1.0.3, node v20.1.0

anjali: i've seen this pattern: autoinstrumentation or the SDK init runs after the retry wrapper in the sampleapp bootstrap. If the wrapper generates request-id early and the SDK later stamps/normalizes it, you can end up with two ids. Also log-level toggles can cause the SDK to defer certain bindings (we do a different init path for debug-level to enable richer hooks).

anjali: quick theory: when REDWOOD_LOG_LEVEL=debug the SDK defers binding to express middleware until otel registers, to avoid double-logging. That deferral path didn't copy the request-id from the temporary header into the reconciled context. hence the apparent "lost" request-id on traces after retries.

maria: workaround i used: explicit require('redwood-telemetry').init({forceSync:true}) at top of app, and keep loglevel=info for onboarding scripts. That keeps request-id steady but loses debug captures. Not ideal. :

liam: can we make a tiny SDK change: if a request-id header exists in the incoming request, stash it on the raw req object before any retry wrapper, and when telemetry finishes init reconcile by preferring existing header? Should be low-risk.

anjali: agree. i'll sketch a patch: on init, look for req.headers['request-id'] || req.headers['x-request-id'] and call context.set('request-id', value) before creating spans. also add test that simulates a retry wrapper and checks header is preserved.

maria: thanks! i'll open a minimal repro repo and a test case for your PR. tagging this as high-impact for onboarding DX, since new users hitting sampleapp with debug on will lose traces and get confusing mismatch.

liam: please include a changelog note and a fallback metric (telemetry:requestid-reconciled) so we can monitor how often reconciliation happens in hosted.

infra-bot: staging-deploy-bot: scheduled redeploy of sampleapp-staging at 2026-03-03T14:00Z for verification :rocket:

maria: added issue #4522 and pushed a tiny repro gist. assigning to @anjali. i'll verify once staging is up. thanks team :thumbsup:
